fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)
fields.rationale: AXI/ACE is a purely digital, synchronous on-chip bus protocol. There are no analog signals, no DC electrical specifications, no AC timing parameters (Vih/Vil/tsu/th/etc.), no IO standards (LVCMOS/LVDS/etc.). The protocol is defined entirely in terms of logical levels sampled on the rising edge of a single clock ACLK.

signaling_summary.clock: Single ACLK per ACE interface (master + interconnect side); all input signals sampled on rising edge of ACLK; all output changes occur after rising edge of ACLK.
signaling_summary.reset: Single active-LOW ARESETn. Async assert, sync deassert.
signaling_summary.io_count: All AXI + ACE channels are unidirectional. No tri-state, no open-drain, no analog.
signaling_summary.default_state_during_reset: Master drives ARVALID/AWVALID/WVALID/CRVALID/CDVALID LOW; interconnect drives RVALID/BVALID/ACVALID LOW; READY signals can default any value (master may default ACREADY HIGH if it can always accept snoops).
signaling_summary.combinatorial_path_rule: On master and slave (and interconnect) interfaces there must be no combinatorial paths between input and output signals. Applies equally to the new ACE snoop channels (AC/CR/CD) — VALID must not be combinationally dependent on READY.

evidence.quote: ACLK (Clock source): Global clock signal. Synchronous signals are sampled on the rising edge of the global clock. ARESETn (Reset source): Global reset signal. This signal is active-LOW.

Each AXI interface has a single clock signal, ACLK. All input signals are sampled on the rising edge of ACLK. All output signal changes can only occur after the rising edge of ACLK. On master and slave interfaces, there must be no combinatorial paths between input and output signals.
The standard AXI VALID/READY handshake rules apply.
The standard AXI VALID/READY handshake rules apply.
